data.description:
## Context / Problem

`compact_rebuild.rebuild_snapshot_under_lock` (`src/rebar/_commands/compact_rebuild.py`, the `fsck --repair-snapshots` path) places its rebuilt SNAPSHOT at `hlc.next_tick(tracker, ticket_id)`, the repair host's clock. The rebuild absorbs every live event it sees and has no horizon. An event another clone wrote between the newest local event and the repair time, not yet fetched, then merges in with a timestamp before the rebuilt SNAPSHOT and is not cited by it: the same `ORPHAN_EVENT` race found in the fold on bug stormproof-stormy-toad.

Found while root-causing stormproof-stormy-toad; that bug fixes only the incremental fold placement.

## Approach

Place the rebuilt SNAPSHOT at the newest absorbed event's timestamp + 1, as the fold does under a positive horizon, so a concurrent unfetched event sorts after it and replays.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A 2-clone test shows an event written on clone B before a repair on clone A replays on A after the merge and fsck reports no `ORPHAN_EVENT`; it fails before the change.
data.title: Snapshot rebuild places SNAPSHOT at repair clock, orphaning unfetched events
